name: Bertolotti Syndrome
definition: Low-back pain associated with a lumbosacral transitional vertebra and a symptomatic pseudoarticulation or altered adjacent-segment biomechanics.

typical: Chronic unilateral or bilateral low-back pain

investigations.principle: Radiographs/CT identify transitional anatomy; MRI evaluates adjacent disc/root pathology.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, tumor, occult injury or condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific imaging pathway.

amber: Diagnostic injections or surgery are selective and require careful correlation.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Kati-shoola phenotype may be documented without equating anatomy to a classical disease.

patientEducation.summary: Low-back pain associated with a lumbosacral transitional vertebra and a symptomatic pseudoarticulation or altered adjacent-segment biomechanics.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, sphincter change, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.
